fields.sample_size: 535 households (262 Lilongwe urban, 273 Lilongwe rural; structured household survey, systematic random sampling, Aug 2024) plus focus group discussions and key-informant interviews (purposive; local chiefs, community leaders, government and NGO water-sector staff)
fields.study_design: mixed-methods case study: cross-sectional household survey (chi-square tests of urban-rural differences) plus FGDs and key-informant interviews, framed by infrastructure violence
fields.effect_estimate: Urban-rural gaps in Lilongwe, Malawi: piped water as main source 90.8% of urban vs 3.66% of rural households (a 87-point gap, wider than the national integrated household survey's 67% vs 6.7%); basic or better service on the JMP ladder 90.08% of urban vs 53.11% of rural households; rural households rely on boreholes and unprotected wells. Chi-square tests of independence for source by area (n = 535); affordability and reliability also assessed. Descriptive comparison, not an effect estimate of a legal or institutional exposure.
fields.section: Full text: Methods (household survey, FGDs, KIIs); Results 3.1-3.4 (Tables 1-3); Discussion 4.1
fields.exact_location: Methods; Results (Tables 1-3, chi-square tests, n = 535); Discussion 4.1

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a mixed-methods case study in Lilongwe, Malawi (535 surveyed households, 262 urban and 273 rural, plus FGDs and key-informant interviews) found piped-water access of 90.8% urban versus 3.66% rural and basic-or-better service of 90.08% versus 53.11%; descriptive urban-rural comparison, read in full text 2026-10-04.
